description: Nigeria accounts for around 40% of obstetric fistula cases worldwide. Of roughly 2 million women globally living with unrepaired vesico-vaginal fistula, about half of the developing-world total were from Nigeria. Prevalence is 3.2 per 1,000 births with an estimated 13,000 new cases annually.
energy_note: Forty per cent of the world's cases, in one country.

description: At current repair rates the backlog of unrepaired cases could take about 83 years to clear. UNICEF has put the number of Nigerian women living with fistula at 400,000 to 800,000; a recent modelling study gives a much lower 45,166.
time_note: Years of living with it, pending a repair queue of decades.
notes: The spread between 45,166 and 400,000-800,000 reflects genuine measurement difficulty, not carelessness. Both are recorded.

description: 80-95% of cases occur when a young woman experiences prolonged obstructed labour without access to a caesarean - the pelvis too small, the head too large, or the baby badly positioned. She may labour five days or more; the baby usually dies; the survivor is left with extensive tissue damage.
energy_note: Five days in labour, and the injury is the survival.

aspect: It is a child-marriage injury as much as an obstetric one
description: A small pelvis is a young pelvis. The states with the highest child marriage rates in WOM-003 are the states with the highest fistula burden, and the causal chain between them is not disputed.
energy_note: Married at fourteen, in obstructed labour at fifteen.

aspect: The social consequence exceeds the medical one
description: Continuous incontinence leads to abandonment by husbands, exclusion from gatherings, and isolation - so the woman loses the household income and the support network at the same moment she acquires a condition requiring both.
energy_note: Divorced, excluded, and leaking, all from one labour.

aspect: The repair exists and is cheap
description: Fistula repair is a well-established surgical procedure with high success rates. The obstacles are the number of surgeons, the distance to them, and knowing the repair exists at all.
energy_note: Fixable, for a few hundred dollars, and mostly not fixed.

aspect: SCENARIO - the woman in the back room
description: She was married at 15 and laboured for four days at 16. She is 34. She has lived in her brother's compound for eighteen years, does not attend the mosque, and has never been told the word for what happened to her or that there is an operation.
energy_note: Eighteen years, for want of being told it was repairable.
